Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the draft order form. A few procurement items we need clarified before legal will sign:

- Invoicing cadence: AlphaTech prefers quarterly invoicing for committed capacity and monthly for overage usage. Can Redwood split the order into quarterly invoices (one per quarter) rather than a single upfront invoice?
- Net terms: our standard is Net45. Please confirm Redwood can accept Net45 for the committed amounts.
- Taxes: who is responsible for sales/VAT? AlphaTech expects to self-account for VAT where applicable; we need the contract to state tax responsibility and any required tax certificates.
- PO: we will need an invoice-able entity and a PO number on the final order form. Can you confirm the billing entity and provide sample invoice header?

If you can send a redline of the order form with those two changes (invoice split + tax clause) I can circulate to Legal for final review. We’re targeting signature this month.

Appreciate it —
Anna

Hi Anna —

Thanks — appreciate the clear list. High level: we can accommodate a split invoicing approach and are open to Net45 for committed spend, with a couple operational caveats below. I’ve attached a redline of the order form (Order_Form_v3_redline.pdf) showing the proposed language. Key points in the redline:

- Invoicing cadence: added Section 2.2.a to allow quarterly invoicing for committed capacity (Jan, Apr, Jul, Oct billing dates) and monthly invoices for usage above commitment. Each invoice will list the PO number when provided.
- Net terms: proposed Net30 by default; agreeing to Net45 for AlphaTech provided the order is invoiced quarterly and the first invoice is issued immediately upon contract effective date. This is to avoid long pre-paid exposure. If Net45 is required for all invoices we can agree subject to a 60-day payment holdback for first quarter only.
- Taxes: added a tax clause clarifying that AlphaTech is responsible for VAT/sales taxes when AlphaTech is the VAT-registered entity and provides appropriate tax certificates. Where law requires Redwood to collect taxes, Redwood will do so and indicate tax on invoice.

Action items for both sides:
- AlphaTech: confirm PO entity and whether tax certificates will be provided for EU/UK jurisdictions.
- Redwood: confirm whether quarterly invoice dates are acceptable and whether finance can accept Net45 with the holdback language if requested.

Looping Karthik for pricing/commits note. I’ll also bring Finance and Legal into the thread after we get your PO details.

Thanks,

Vanessa / team — forwarding Anna’s note and the redline. Quick thoughts from GTM side:

- Pricing / commits: AlphaTech is committed to a $1.2M annual committed spend per our SOW. We can do quarterly invoices at $300k/quarter for the committed portion. For overages, invoices will be monthly. If they want Net45 across the board we will absorb incremental AR risk only if Finance signs off (see marissa).
- Minimum commit crediting: propose that any unused committed spend at quarter end rolls forward as a credit against future usage for up to two quarters (we don’t want long-term refunds). I added markup in the redline.
- Taxes: generally we expect customers in the US to pay sales/use taxes where applicable; for EU customers AlphaTech will provide local VAT registration and tax certificates. Stephanie — can you confirm whether the tax clause language Vanessa proposed is sufficient? Also flag any need for tax certificates or W-9/FTIN equivalents.

Marissa — can Finance accept Net45 for quarterly invoices with a one-quarter holdback if necessary? If not, we should be explicit in the order form that Net30 is Redwood’s default and Net45 requires approval.

thanks —
